Section 1: The Premise of the Company

Joint Stock Company Kaspi.kz (NASDAQ: KSPI) operates an ultra-dominant, multi-sided digital ecosystem in Central Asia and is aggressively expanding into Türkiye. Structured around its consumer Super App and merchant Kaspi Pay platform, the company seamlessly integrates three high-frequency operating pillars: Marketplace (e-commerce, commercial catalog, travel, and logistics), Payments (P2P transfers, QR payments, bill payments, and merchant acquiring), and Fintech (BNPL, merchant trade finance, consumer loans, and deposits). By embedding itself into the daily economic fabric of Kazakhstan—where its consumer app reaches 15.7 million Monthly Active Users (MAU) out of an adult population of ~12 million, with an industry-leading Daily Active User (DAU) to MAU ratio of 68%—Kaspi.kz functions as a national economic tollbooth and digital highway.

Core Business Model, Unit Monetization & Growth Engine

Kaspi’s flywheel relies on extreme transaction frequency and zero-friction cross-platform monetization:

  • Payments Platform: Monetized via merchant processing fees (taking ~1.00%–1.07% on Total Payment Volume, or TPV) and interest earned on float held within term deposits ($80M+ annually). Payments serve as the low-friction acquisition funnel, driving consumer engagement to 77 transactions per active user per month.
  • Marketplace Platform: Monetized through seller take rates averaging 12.1% (expanding +110 bps YoY driven by high-margin value-added services like Kaspi Advertising and Kaspi Delivery) on Gross Merchandise Value (GMV). In 2025, Kaspi acquired an 85.17% controlling stake in Hepsiburada (D-MARKET Electronic Services), extending its marketplace model into Türkiye’s 85+ million population market.
  • Fintech Platform: Monetized through net interest margin (NIM) and fee revenue generated on Total Finance Volume (TFV), predominantly driven by short-duration (average maturity <6 months), high-velocity BNPL (Kaspi Red) and merchant working capital loans. Loan origination is funded by sticky, low-cost retail deposits held inside the Kaspi Super App.

Trailing 4-Quarter Earnings & Operational Commentary

Across the last four reported quarters (Q3 2025 through Q2 2026), Kaspi.kz demonstrated strong top-line compounding alongside disciplined balance sheet management, while navigating the near-term dilution of its Turkish expansion:

  • Q3 2025: Delivered KZT 1.12 trillion ($2.22B USD) in total revenue (+51% YoY), driven by the initial consolidation of Hepsiburada and a 51% surge in quarterly interest income. Net profit reached KZT 270B ($534M USD), as elevated base rates increased bank deposit funding costs.
  • Q4 2025: Concluded FY2025 with full-year revenue reaching $8,004M USD (+59.8% YoY) and net profit holding firm at $2,112M USD (+1.0% YoY). Marketplace GMV growth accelerated to +28% YoY on a constant currency basis, while Hepsiburada approached operational EBITDA breakeven ahead of management guidance.
  • Q1 2026: Revenue rose 31% YoY to KZT 1.08 trillion ($2.26B USD), led by Marketplace revenue of $1.08B USD (+58% YoY). Adjusted EBITDA expanded to $769M USD (+9% YoY). The company secured regulatory approval for its acquisition of Rabobank A.Ş. in Türkiye, laying the infrastructure for launching Kaspi Fintech products in Türkiye by 2027.
  • Q2 2026: Reported consolidated revenue of $2.30B USD (+15% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $826M USD (+5% YoY). E-commerce GMV surged 28% YoY on a constant currency basis with annual purchases per consumer expanding to 15.8x. Management unveiled Kasper, an integrated AI shopping assistant, and recommended an 18% QoQ dividend step-up to KZT 1,000 per ADS.

Governance, Executive Control & C-Suite Audit

Kaspi.kz maintains high insider alignment and key-person stability. Co-Founder and CEO Mikheil Lomtadze and Non-Executive Chairman Vyacheslav Kim remain the primary strategic drivers, collectively controlling over 40% of voting equity. In early 2026, global technology conglomerate Tencent acquired a strategic equity stake alongside CEO Mikheil Lomtadze, validating Kaspi's Super App architecture.

Activist & Short-Seller Audit: In September 2024, short-seller Culper Research published a report alleging sanctions evasion and non-operating revenue inflation. Kaspi’s board and independent audit committee conducted an immediate review, issuing detailed factual rebuttals. Independent auditor Deloitte LLP issued an unmodified, clean audit opinion on Kaspi’s FY2025 Form 20-F (filed March 16, 2026), affirming internal financial controls and regulatory compliance.

Economic Moat Classification: Wide Moat

Kaspi.kz commands an insurmountable Wide Moat derived from structural multi-sided network effects, extreme ecosystem lock-in, and infrastructure scale density:

  • Multi-Sided Network Effects: 15.7 million consumers and 764,000 active merchants create an entrenched virtuous cycle. Merchant coverage is so dense that Kaspi Pay is the default national transaction standard in Kazakhstan.
  • High Switching Costs: Consumers store primary savings, receive salaries, pay bills, buy retail products, and book travel exclusively inside the Super App. Merchants rely on Kaspi for point-of-sale hardware, working capital credit, inventory listing, and last-mile delivery.
  • Cost Advantage & Tollbooth Status: Proprietary closed-loop payment rails bypass international card networks, driving customer acquisition costs (CAC) near zero and enabling mid-30s net profit margins.

True maintenance CapEx is strictly anchored to statutory Depreciation & Amortization (~30% of total CapEx), representing the capital required to maintain core IT software, server fleets, and POS hardware.

Fundamental Compounding Velocity & Pricing Power Audit

  • Return on Invested Capital (ROIC): 31.2% in FY2025 (and historical ROE exceeding 40%), demonstrating extraordinary capital efficiency and pricing power across closed-loop payment and marketplace platforms.
  • Take Rate Expansion: Marketplace take rate expanded +110 bps YoY to 12.1% in Q2 2026, proving merchant willingness to pay for high-converting ecosystem services (Kaspi Delivery, Kaspi Advertising).
  • Ecosystem Frequency: 77 monthly transactions per active consumer, providing an unrivaled low-cost funding base and robust credit data underwriting advantage.

Section 2: The Probable Future Paths

Based on the company's audited statutory filings, segment dynamics, 4-quarter earnings call commentary, and institutional counter-theses, here are the distinct, realistic operational paths covering 90%–95% of the fundamental probability space over the next 3–5 years:

Path 1: Central Baseline Continuation & Super App Regional Compounding

Archetype: Central Baseline Trend & Operational Continuation

Overview: Kaspi.kz leverages its dominant Kazakh Super App flywheel—integrating Payments, Marketplace, and Fintech—alongside a disciplined integration of Hepsiburada in Türkiye. Revenue compounds at a +17.9% CAGR over 5 years, supported by high platform user engagement, rising GMV monetization, and controlled credit provisioning. Operating margins normalize around 31.5%–32.5% as Turkish expansion dilutes margins initially before cross-border synergies take hold. Year-5 Owner Earnings per share reach $16.61 (representing a +22.8% per-share OE CAGR from OE&₀ of $5.94). Applying a conservative 15.0x terminal multiple plus $4.49 net cash yields a 5-year target price of $253.64 ($161.12 Present Intrinsic Fair Value at a 9.5% discount rate).

Path 2: Turkish Integration Friction, Core Maturation & Regional FX Margin Drag

Archetype: Downside Friction, Competitive Headwinds & Margin Drag

Overview: Kaspi encounters market saturation in its core Kazakh domestic footprint while the integration of Hepsiburada in Türkiye faces severe macro volatility, Turkish Lira depreciation, and aggressive competitive response from local e-commerce players (e.g., Trendyol). Operating margins compress to 27.0% due to higher fulfillment costs, elevated promotional spend, and sticky funding costs in the Fintech segment. Top-line revenue growth slows to a +14.1% CAGR, yielding Year-5 Owner Earnings per share of $9.71 (+10.3% per-share OE CAGR). Under an 11.0x multiple (reflecting elevated regional risk and lower ROIC), plus $4.49 net cash per share, the 5-year target price is $111.35 ($70.73 Present Intrinsic Fair Value).

Path 3: Turkish Cross-Border Flywheel & Super App Monetization Supercycle

Archetype: Upside Acceleration, Operating Leverage & TAM Expansion

Overview: Kaspi executes a masterclass expansion into Türkiye, turning Hepsiburada into a high-margin marketplace and cross-border trade engine linking Central Asia and the Mediterranean. Domestic Kazakh Super App monetization accelerates through high-margin merchant services, advertising, and delivery solutions, driving operating margins up to 37.5%. Revenue grows at a +26.3% 5-year CAGR, driving Year-5 Owner Earnings to $28.38 per share (+36.7% per-share OE CAGR). Applying an 18.0x terminal multiple to reflect high structural ROIC (38.7%) and an expanded TAM yields a 5-year target price of $515.33 ($327.35 Present Intrinsic Fair Value).

Section 3:Normalized Owner Earnings Multiple & Yield Inversion Valuation

To establish a rigorous fundamental valuation for Joint Stock Company Kaspi.kz, we evaluate owner earnings cash flow generation across three distinct operational paths over a 5-year horizon (2026–2031). Starting from an Audited Baseline Owner Earnings per share of $5.94 (GAAP Operating Cash Flow minus Maintenance CapEx anchored to D&A minus 100% Stock-Based Compensation), each trajectory incorporates sector-specific capital intensity, credit provisioning expectations, and international expansion execution. Terminal valuations are capitalized using economic growth-calibrated P/OE multiples plus a balance sheet cash adjustment of +$4.49 per share, discounted to present value at a strict 9.5% equity hurdle rate.

Empirical Probability Weighting Rationale

Path 1 (Central Baseline - 55% Weight): Kaspi's unassailable Wide Moat in Kazakhstan—where over 65% of the adult population engages daily with its Super App—provides exceptional recurring cash flow visibility. High ROIC (31.2%) and entrenched multi-sided network effects warrant assigning the majority of probability mass to steady-state regional compounding.

Path 2 (Downside Friction - 25% Weight): Assigned a substantial 25% weight to account for macro headwinds in Türkiye (currency devaluation, elevated inflation), domestic Kazakh market saturation risk, and potential friction in scaling cross-border logistics without diluting cash margins.

Path 3 (Upside Supercycle - 20% Weight): Captures the upside option value of successful Turkish market penetration via Hepsiburada, transforming Kaspi into a multi-country Super App power with expanding marketplace take rates and international trade flows.

Market Inversion & Valuation Synthesis

Implied Market Reality: At today's market price of $105.38, the market is pricing Joint Stock Company Kaspi.kz at 17.74x Normalized Owner Earnings (an implied Owner Cash Yield of 5.6%). After subtracting $4.49/share of balance sheet net cash, Mr. Market is valuing Kaspi's operating business at $100.89/share. Assuming a baseline exit multiple of 15.0x, today's stock price implies that Kaspi only needs to grow Owner Earnings at a mere +2.5% per year over the next 5 years (to $6.73 OE/share by Year 5). Even under a static 17.74x multiple, the market requires a -0.9% CAGR. This is an extraordinarily low bar for a high-return business expanding across Central Asia.

Probability-Weighted 5-Year Target Price: $270.41 / share (Expected 5-Year Annualized CAGR: +20.7% / yr).

Probability-Weighted Present Fair Value (9.5% Hurdle): $171.77 / share (Margin of Safety: +63.0% vs. today's market price of $105.38).

Capital Allocation Recommendation: BUY. Kaspi offers an outstanding risk-adjusted entry point with a +63.0% Margin of Safety above current quotations. Even under our conservative Downside Sensitivity scenario (45% weight on Turkish friction/macro drag), the intrinsic value of $137.07 provides a +30.1% buffer. The asymmetric risk/reward profile is heavily skewed to the upside.
